subject: Next steps & security evidence — stakeholder mapping for Redwood evaluation
messages: Subject: Next steps & security evidence — stakeholder mapping for Redwood evaluation

Hi Alex,

Great to meet earlier today — thanks for taking the time to demo the current flow and walk through the latency/cost constraints for your transaction enrichment pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: Replace current inference path for enrichment with a more predictable, lower-cost runtime while maintaining P95 latency <= 120ms.
- Key decision criteria you called out: latency SLO, data residency/compliance, and unit TCO.
- Primary stakeholders you indicated on the call: you (platform lead), Lauren Chen (procurement), and your Security/Legal team (TBD contact).

Action items I propose:
1) Stakeholder mapping: can you confirm the primary security/legal contact (name + email) and whether procurement needs an initial quote or a redline SLA?
2) Security evidence: we can provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary, sample audit logs, and our data retention policy. Let me know which are needed and we’ll send over the artifacts (PDFs/CSV stub).
3) Timeline: If procurement/Legal want copies up-front, we’ll push the SOC2 + pen test today and follow with audit log extract (sanitized) and retention answers by next Tuesday.

If that schedule works, I’ll loop in Marissa (CS lead) and Evelyn from Legal to coordinate any contract/procurement questions.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Next steps & security evidence — stakeholder mapping for Redwood evaluation

Jordan — thanks for the recap and very useful call. Confirming a few items: 

- Stakeholders: I’m the technical owner and will drive the evaluation. Security lead is Maria Gonzales (maria.gonzales@fintegrity.com) — I’d like her included on the next exchange. Procurement is Lauren Chen (cc’d).
- Decision criteria: correct — latency and TCO, plus we need clear answers on data retention and where PII is stored/encrypted. Also need to confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

For procurement: we’ll need SOC 2 Type II and either a high-level pen test summary or a redacted report. If you can also provide a sample of the kind of audit logs we’d receive (schema + sample rows), that would speed our compliance review.

Can you send the SOC2 + pen test summary to me and Maria? Procurement will ask for an initial quote but they can wait until we confirm the technical fit.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Smith
Platform Lead, Fintegrity Labs
alex.smith@fintegrity.com | (617) 555-9988

Hi Alex / Maria / Lauren — looping in Evelyn from Legal to help with any contract/procurement redlines. Per Jordan’s note, attached are the artifacts you requested:

Attachments (stubs):
- Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf — full report (redacted PII where required).
- PenTest_Summary_2025.pdf — executive summary of the most recent third-party assessment. Full report available under NDA; happy to coordinate if Maria needs it.
- AuditLogs_Sample.csv — sanitized sample showing timestamp, request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, region.
- DataRetention_Policy.txt — short policy doc describing retention windows and deletion controls.

Answers to quick questions you raised:
- Customer-managed KMS: supported in our Private deployment; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK options for enterprise contracts. Evelyn can confirm contract language.
- PII storage: Redwood does not persist raw customer PII as part of the inference runtime; any logs are pseudonymized and encrypted at rest. See attached DataRetention_Policy for retention windows.

Next steps we propose:
1) We’ll share the HubSpot deal + artifacts link here (Doc link below).
2) Maria — if you’d like the full pen test report, please confirm an NDA and we’ll route the vendor report via secure share.
3) Lauren — when you’re ready, we can provide a one-page pricing estimate for dedicated capacity vs. hosted (monthly commit options).
